capability_rows.claim: FBS removes sgtin with one DELETE /api/v3/orders/{orderId}/meta?key=sgtin request per order.
No FBS batch-delete endpoint is documented; mass deletion is a WMS queue of single-order requests. The official FBS batch change applies to metadata reads up to 100 IDs.
HTTP 204 confirms deletion for that order only and has no response body.

The key=sgtin DELETE removes the complete sgtin value for one order. That value is an array of 1..100 marking codes, so a selected subset is rejected before any remote call; only a selection proven equal to the full snapshotted array is eligible for delete-all.
The quota is seller-account scoped and shared by all FBS metadata get/delete methods, so API and workers must coordinate one limiter for that seller and method group.
The documented standard method profile is 300 requests per minute, 200 ms interval and burst 20; token types can have reduced profiles.
Every 4XX response for this endpoint consumes ten request units and must affect the shared limiter state, even when the per-order outcome is terminal rather than retryable.
Non-429 responses expose X-Ratelimit-Remaining; 429 exposes X-Ratelimit-Retry, X-Ratelimit-Reset and X-Ratelimit-Limit. Retry-After is not the named WB 429 contract.
A 429 item cannot retry before X-Ratelimit-Retry; repeated 429 responses increase the delay and retries must stop after a finite 3-5-attempt policy.
Missing, negative or non-numeric WB retry headers must not cause immediate retry; S13 must choose a safe finite fallback delay.

Partial success exists across the local mass operation, but not inside one key=sgtin DELETE: one 204 confirms delete-all for that order's full snapshotted sgtin array, while 429 or failure on one order does not roll back or authorize another order.
Timeout, transport failure, 5xx or worker crash after send does not prove whether DELETE took effect and requires read-back before another delete or local clearing.

Persist a hash and outcome for every code in the full pre-delete array. Read-back of the whole array maps only full absence to REMOVED_AS_PART_OF_DELETE_ALL and full presence to STILL_PRESENT_RETRY_ELIGIBLE; a mixed, unknown or changed array is fail-closed review for every affected code.
POST /api/marketplace/v3/orders/meta reads up to 100 FBS orders and is the documented read-back surface; use current metaDetails, not legacy meta.
Local KIZ binding cannot be cleared until a 204 or unambiguous read-back confirms remote deletion for the current marking revision.
400, 401, 402, 403 and 409 are not rate-limit retries; they require correction, access handling or final per-order failure, while every 4XX still debits ten limiter units.
No quota-restored webhook is documented; the WMS scheduler resumes at next_attempt_at without frequent active polling.
Progress and limiter state are tenant/seller isolated; token values, raw KIZ and raw response bodies are excluded from operator output and ordinary logs.
The operator needs per-operation counts and an exact final list of unprocessed orders; manual retry cannot bypass the limiter or next_attempt_at.
Five hundred single-order delete-all calls require at least about 100 seconds at 200 ms with no competing calls, retries, read-back or weighted 4XX errors; this is a lower bound, not an SLA.
DELETE is single-order and metadata read-back is a bounded batch without a pagination token.
The narrow external-call change concerns FBS order marking metadata only and does not change catalog, stock, reserve, print, cancel or return contracts.
BLG-I19 is a narrow change to an existing FBS external call, not a new domain, module, FBO process or competitor-screen research task.

Deterministic emulator cases are required at S15/S23; no live WB or WB sandbox call is needed or authorized in S03. Any future Marketplace sandbox case uses an independent limiter of at most one request per second across all methods.
